options.description: Each question the checker raises is asked as it comes, merged by principle and in plain words. The agent does not send questions back for withdrawal, and nothing is dropped before you see it. Recommended: Your words ask for the notice to go and questions to be asked on the spot, with no cap. Asking straight away matches that most directly. The send-back loop adds a step you did not describe.
options.label: Ask straight away (Recommended)

options.description: If the agent thinks a question is already answered, it sends it back with its reason, and the checker withdraws it or keeps it. Only kept questions reach you, and the log shows every send-back.
options.label: Send obvious ones back

options.description: You describe in your own words how questions should be handled; nothing beyond that is built.
options.label: Simplify differently

payload.question:
When a question seems obvious or already answered by what you said, should the agent send it back for review, or simply ask it straight away?

You said on 2026-10-26: "I wonder if that feature has become cumbersome and outdated and should be deleted?"
